note: Regenerate with gen_vectors.py. A Rust implementation of artifact@1 must reproduce every hash below byte for byte. Where the two disagree, THESE are the contract and both implementations are suspect until one is shown to violate the schema.

vectors.name: baseline
vectors.why: the unmutated example; every other vector is measured against it

vectors.name: lexical_engine_revision
vectors.why: an engine upgrade is a new physical artifact of the SAME logical version -- this is the property that lets a session pin survive an engine promotion

vectors.name: envelope_format_version
vectors.why: the envelope format is physical; a reader-compatibility change must not force a reindex

vectors.name: vector_kind_approximate
vectors.why: exact-vs-approximate is a binding change, recorded in the plan and never in the logical id

vectors.name: source_content_hash
vectors.why: different bytes in a source are a different corpus

vectors.name: source_order
vectors.why: source order is part of the identity: the builder streams in this order, so two builds of the same SET that disagree by permutation are not the same build

vectors.name: chunker_param
vectors.why: a resolved chunker parameter changes the chunks, so it changes results

vectors.name: extractor_outcome
vectors.why: per-source extracted text is what got indexed; without it two builds whose extraction silently differed would share a logical id

vectors.name: analyzer_tokenizer
vectors.why: the documented V1 decision in force: the analyzer contract is a result-affecting input, so a tokenizer change produces a new logical version that must be activated like any corpus change. The corpus-only alternative is recorded in decisions.md with its trigger.

vectors.name: analyzer_stop_terms
vectors.why: the stop list is carried by HASH, not by reference alone -- a reference would let the list change under a fixed logical id

vectors.name: embedder_model
vectors.why: a different embedder ranks differently; the provenance envelope's index_version is what an audit uses to say how an answer was ranked

vectors.name: embedder_absent
vectors.why: a lexical-only corpus is valid and is NOT the same logical corpus as a hybrid one

vectors.name: snapshot_watermark
vectors.why: the same sources at a different watermark is a different snapshot

vectors.name: key_order_permuted
vectors.why: the same content with object members written in a different order canonicalizes to the SAME bytes -- this is the whole point of JCS key ordering

vectors.name: probe_order_is_content
vectors.why: ARRAY order is content, unlike object member order: reordering probes is a different manifest, because an array is a sequence and canonicalization does not sort it

must_refuse.name: float_in_document
must_refuse.why: artifact@1 forbids floating-point numbers; a canonicalizer must refuse rather than format one. See canonicalization.schema.json why_no_floats.

must_refuse.name: manifest_with_build_timestamp
must_refuse.why: the manifest is content-pure. A builder that stamps built_at makes byte-identical rebuilds collide instead of converging, which is the defect the purity rule exists to prevent. additionalProperties:false must reject it.

must_refuse.name: manifest_with_tenant_id
must_refuse.why: tenant is authority, not content. An identical corpus in two tenants legitimately produces one artifact_id; isolation lives in the catalog key and the runtime ArtifactCacheKey. Putting it here would make a content hash pretend to be an authorization boundary.

must_refuse.name: component_path_traversal
must_refuse.why: component paths are normalized relative paths; '..' escapes the artifact prefix
must_refuse.document_note: the baseline manifest with a component path of "../../etc/passwd"

must_refuse.name: component_path_absolute
must_refuse.why: an absolute path ignores the artifact root entirely
must_refuse.document_note: the baseline manifest with a component path of "/etc/passwd"
